analysis: The question asks to identify an uricosuric drug among the given options. Uricosuric drugs are agents that increase the excretion of uric acid in the urine, thus lowering the levels of uric acid in the blood. Probenecid is a well-known uricosuric drug used primarily to treat gout by increasing the renal excretion of uric acid. Allopurinol, while used in the management of gout, is not an uricosuric drug but rather a xanthine oxidase inhibitor that reduces the production of uric acid. Indomethacin is an anti-inflammatory drug and not primarily used for its uricosuric action. Aspirin at low doses can reduce uric acid excretion and at very high doses has a weak uricosuric effect, but it is not primarily classified or used as an uricosuric agent. Therefore, based on standard pharmacological classifications, Probenecid is the correct answer.
